interest: Tax-reciprocity docket reveals Japanese Navy and Army procurement missions in New York and early espionage surveillance.
overview: This file comprises sheets 11 through 36 of the Department of State's official 'List of Papers' (purport and docket register) for decimal file 894.01 B 11 (catalogued under subject 'Agents of Japan in the United States'), covering correspondence from May 1936 through December 1939 (sub-numbers 60 to 214). The register records diplomatic notes and inter-departmental communications between the Japanese Embassy in Washington, the Department of State (principally the Division of Far Eastern Affairs and the Legal Adviser), and the Treasury Department (Bureau of Internal Revenue), establishing and administering reciprocal income tax exemptions on official salaries under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1936. Dozens of Japanese personnel are tracked in detail, including technical officers and inspectors of the Imperial Japanese Navy and Army Ordnance offices in New York City, officials of the Japanese Government Railways, silk and agricultural experts, Board of Tourist Industry representatives, and architects for the 1939 New York and San Francisco international expositions. In addition to tax certifications and port-departure clearances, the register documents State Department inquiries into Japanese commercial propaganda, efforts to counter American boycotts, registrations under the 1938 Foreign Agents Registration Act, legal retainers for Japanese consulates, and a Department of Justice espionage investigation.

subfiles.about: A continuous 26-page Department of State purport list registering diplomatic notes, official correspondence, and memoranda concerning Japanese agents, officials, and reciprocal tax exemptions in the United States from May 1936 to December 1939.
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Communications and Records
keywords: Agents of Japan in the United States
subfiles.summary: This 26-page docket sheet registers correspondence sub-numbers 60 through 214 of State Department decimal file 894.01 B 11 between May 15, 1936, and December 28, 1939. The overwhelming majority of entries record requests by the Japanese Embassy in Washington for Federal income tax exemptions on the official compensation of Japanese non-diplomatic personnel, including naval and military inspectors, railway representatives, agricultural and silk experts, exposition commissioners, and language officers. It details the administrative clearance process across the Department of State, the Treasury Department's Bureau of Internal Revenue, and port collectors in New York, San Francisco, Los Angeles, and Seattle, alongside reciprocal reporting obligations for American officials residing in Japan. Interspersed among the tax records are entries concerning Japanese commercial trade organizations, anti-boycott propaganda committees, foreign agent registrations, legal retainers for Japanese consular posts, and a Department of Justice espionage inquiry.
